title: Modi Pledges 'New Arsenal of Reforms' at ET World Leaders Forum as India Eyes 20% of Global Growth
excerpt: At The Economic Times summit in New Delhi, the Prime Minister highlighted India's 90% economic expansion over a decade and outlined plans for sweeping policy changes across sectors.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed The Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026 in New Delhi, pledging a "new arsenal of reforms" to sustain India's position as the world's fastest-growing major economy.
  • Modi cited India's economy growing 90% over the past decade compared to 35% for the global economy, with the IMF projecting 6.4% growth this fiscal year.
  • India's fiscal deficit is expected to decline to 4.4%, and the country received its first credit rating upgrade from S&P Global in nearly two decades.
  • The Prime Minister pointed to record formal job creation of 2.2 million in June and said India is poised to contribute nearly 20% of global growth.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi used his address at The Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026 to lay out an ambitious reform agenda, telling an audience of industrialists, global investors, and policymakers at the Taj Palace in New Delhi that India is ready to unleash a fresh wave of policy changes to cement its status as a global economic powerhouse.

The two-day forum, held August 21-22, brought together prominent business leaders and thought leaders from India and abroad. Modi's keynote address was the summit's marquee event, with markets and policy watchers listening closely for signals on the government's next phase of economic reforms.

India's Economic Record Under the Spotlight

Modi opened with a pointed comparison: while the global economy grew 35% over the past decade, India's economy expanded by nearly 90%. He framed this as sustained, structural growth rather than a cyclical uptick, and pledged it would continue.

"With the mantra of 'reform, perform, transform,' Bharat today is in a position to help the world emerge from slow growth. We are not people who sit on the shore by stagnant waters, throwing stones for amusement — we are the people who change the course of gushing rivers."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ET World Leaders Forum 2026

The International Monetary Fund expects India's economy to expand 6.4% this fiscal year, maintaining its position as the fastest-growing major economy. Modi also highlighted India's first credit rating upgrade from Standard & Poor's Global in nearly two decades, and a fiscal deficit on track to fall to 4.4%.

On employment, the Prime Minister cited EPFO data showing 2.2 million formal jobs were added in India in June alone — an all-time high — while retail inflation stood at its lowest level since 2017 and foreign exchange reserves hit a record.

A 'New Arsenal of Reforms'

Moving beyond backward-looking metrics, Modi signaled that his government is preparing a sweeping new reform push. He outlined several fronts of action: eliminating unnecessary laws, simplifying rules and procedures, digitizing processes and approvals, and decriminalizing provisions across sectors.

"Reforms are neither a compulsion, nor crisis-driven for us," Modi said. "They are our commitment and conviction. With a holistic approach, we deeply review one sector, and then carry out reforms in that sector, one by one."

He pointed to recent legislative progress, including GST 2.0 and the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill, as evidence of continued momentum. Modi also referenced the Jan Vishwas 2.0 bill and new laws on mining, ports, and shipping passed during the monsoon session of Parliament, along with a forthcoming national sports policy.

Self-Reliance and Semiconductors

Modi reiterated his vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat — self-reliant India — as the foundation for achieving Viksit Bharat (developed India) by 2047. He criticized previous governments for "missing the bus" on technology and industry revolutions, particularly during the internet and communications eras.

India has since built 5G infrastructure indigenously and is set to begin semiconductor manufacturing by year-end, Modi said, marking a transformation in the country's technology ambitions. The government has pursued aggressive semiconductor initiatives, with multiple fabrication facilities now moving into production.

What It Means for the Diaspora and Global Investors

For NRIs and global investors, Modi's address reinforced the themes that have made India an increasingly watched investment destination: policy stability, regulatory reform, infrastructure investment, and a young workforce. The government's focus on ease of doing business and attracting global capital has been central to this pitch.

"Through its resilience and strength, Bharat has become a symbol of hope for the rest of the world."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi

Manufacturing remains at the center of the government's economic strategy, backed by Production-Linked Incentive schemes, digital public infrastructure, defense manufacturing, and logistics modernization. Modi emphasized that India is on track to become the world's third-largest economy, with experts projecting the country will contribute nearly a fifth of global growth in the coming years.

The forum comes at a significant moment for India on the global stage. With the U.S. economy navigating fiscal pressures and China's growth slowing, India's sustained expansion has drawn increasing attention from multinational corporations and institutional investors looking to diversify their exposure to emerging markets.
